text:
Marissa Cole: Need alignment on Console UX for auto-rollback. Specifically: (1) how we show the current “verdict” from SLO evaluator, (2) how we display rollback reason(s), (3) manual override/ack flows. Want to lock this this week so Kenji can finalize the rollout page.

Kenji Nakamura: Dropping WIP frames (Figma) in a sec. I’m currently showing a “Health verdict” pill on the rollout header + a side panel with details.

Kenji Nakamura: Figma: https://figma.com/file/ri-autorollback-verdict-v1 (wip) 
- header pill: Healthy / Warning / Breach / Rolling back / Rolled back / Unknown
- “View details” opens drawer: monitors, thresholds, current values, window, min traffic, cooldown

Paula Mendes: +1 on having “Unknown” as first-class. We’ve been burned by “no data” looking like “healthy.”

Chloe Martin: Agree. Also we need to be careful about naming: “Warning” vs “Degraded” vs “At risk” (SRE will have opinions). For API we’re calling it verdict: HEALTHY | DEGRADED | BREACHED | ROLLBACK_IN_PROGRESS | ROLLED_BACK | UNKNOWN.

Jada Williams: From backend perspective we can provide:
- verdict enum
- reasons[] (each reason has monitor identity + comparison result)
- trace id for decision
But the console shouldn’t overfit to internal structure. We should show a small set of “reason codes” and then a “see monitors” section.

Felix Schneider: What are we thinking for “reason” strings? Users will ask “why did it rollback” and we need something consistent for audit history.

Paula Mendes: Proposed high-level reason categories:
1) Latency SLO breach
2) Error-rate SLO breach
3) Baseline regression (must be worse than baseline)
4) Safeguard: low traffic (no action)
5) Safeguard: warm-up window (no action)
6) Monitoring unavailable/stale (Unknown)
Then a detail line like: “p95 latency 1.8s > 1.2s for 10m (min 500 req)” with links.

Kenji Nakamura: In the drawer I currently show “Primary reason” with the first failing condition, then “Other signals” collapsed.

Marissa Cole: Do we want “primary reason” always? Concern: users get confused when both latency+errors are failing.

Chloe Martin: I’d rather list both and use a simple ordering (Errors > Latency > Baseline compare). “Primary” implies we’re choosing causality.

Jada Williams: +1. The evaluator can return multiple breached conditions. We can label “Triggered by” and show bullet list.

Dylan Brooks: Also keep in mind support workflows: they’ll screenshot the rollout page. We should include the evaluation window, region, tier, route, model version in the summary so it’s not buried.

Hannah Rivera: For notifications (Slack incident-bot) we’ll need a consistent string too. If Console shows “Triggered by: Error-rate breach (5xx)” we can mirror that.

Marissa Cole: OK, so verdict pill + “Triggered by” list. Next question: where do we put manual override/ack? Product requirement is: operator can pause auto-rollback OR acknowledge a rollback event.

Paula Mendes: Important nuance: “ack” is not “disable.” Ack is for human confirmation + audit trail (“we saw it”). Pause disables future automated actions for that rollout policy for some duration.

Kenji Nakamura: UI idea:
- When verdict is BREACHED or ROLLBACK_* show a banner with two actions: [Acknowledge] [Pause auto-rollback]
- Acknowledge opens modal with optional note
- Pause opens modal: duration + note (required?)

Naomi Feldman: For compliance/audit, “Pause” and “Override” actions should require a reason/comment. Ack can be optional but must record who did it and when.

Chloe Martin: Backend can enforce note required on pause. For ack we’ll store acked_by + acked_at + ack_note.

Felix Schneider: Also we should be explicit about what “Pause” affects. Does it pause only this rollout (current canary), or all future rollouts for the route/model? My assumption is per-rollout instance.

Paula Mendes: Per rollout policy instance / active rollout, not globally. Separate control for policy edit.

Jada Williams: Implementation detail: we have rollout_id, policy_id. “Pause” sets a flag on rollout state (e.g. auto_rollback_disabled_until). It shouldn’t change the stored policy. We can display “Paused until <ts>” in the drawer.

Marissa Cole: Yes. Pause is operational.

Dylan Brooks: Request: add “Manual rollback now” button? (even if out of scope) I keep seeing this asked.

Marissa Cole: Not in scope for this project. We can add “Rollback now” later as separate story. For now only auto rollback and manual pause/ack.

Kenji Nakamura: Cool. For the timeline/history, I’m showing events:
- Policy evaluated: Healthy/Degraded/Breached
- Auto rollback triggered
- Traffic split reverted to <previous version>
- Cooldown started
- Operator acked
- Operator paused

Chloe Martin: That maps to API events we’re adding anyway. Just be careful: “Policy evaluated” might be super noisy. Maybe only show state transitions + actions.

Paula Mendes: +1. Only log when verdict changes or when action is taken. Otherwise timeline is unreadable.

Jada Williams: We’ll emit a “verdict_changed” event with from/to + reasons hash. Console can render only those.

Hannah Rivera: For Slack notifications: I’d like a link to the exact drawer state (verdict details) + runbook. Can we have a stable URL with rollout_id + “tab=verdict”?

Chloe Martin: Yes. We can add query param to open the drawer. Also runbook link can be a constant field in response (or computed by console).

Kenji Nakamura: How should “Unknown” look? Right now it’s gray pill + text “Monitoring data unavailable.”

Paula Mendes: And critically: Unknown should not show “No issues detected.” Maybe show “Cannot determine health” + “Auto rollback behavior: <fail-open/fail-closed>”.

Marissa Cole: Great point. We need to be transparent. But do we show fail-open/closed in UI? Might be too much.

Jada Williams: We can show a simple line: “Automated actions are paused while monitoring is unavailable” vs “Automated actions may still occur based on last known good data” depending on config. (Though our current default is fail-open = don’t rollback on unknown.)

Chloe Martin: Let’s keep it minimal: for Unknown, show:
- “Monitor data unavailable or stale”
- “No automated rollback action taken” (if that’s true)
Then in advanced section show “Behavior: fail-open” for those who care.

Naomi Feldman: Please ensure the audit history differentiates “Unknown verdict” vs “Healthy.” We’ve had auditors ask “why didn’t you act” and the answer was “we couldn’t see metrics.”

Felix Schneider: For the reason display in history, suggest we store reason codes so translations/string tweaks don’t break historical meaning.

Chloe Martin: Agreed. Console can render reason_code -> label.

Kenji Nakamura: I’ll adjust copy:
- DEGRADED => “Degraded” instead of “Warning”
- BREACHED => “SLO breached”
- UNKNOWN => “No verdict (monitoring unavailable)”
Actions only appear for Breached/Rollback*/Unknown? (pause should be possible even when Healthy?)

Paula Mendes: Pause should be available always (some customers want to disable before a risky deploy). But we can tuck it under overflow menu when Healthy to avoid scary UI.

Marissa Cole: +1. Overflow “•••” -> “Pause auto-rollback…” always available.

Dylan Brooks: Ack should only appear when something happened (breach/rollback). Otherwise you’ll get random acks.

Hannah Rivera: Also if rollback happened, ack should show in Slack thread? like ConsoleBot posts “Acked by X”. Not required for MVP but would help oncall.

Chloe Martin: Not MVP. But we can emit event and incident-bot can subscribe later.

ConsoleBot: (system) Reminder: Console/Rollouts design review scheduled Thu 11:00 PT. Please add links to relevant frames and open questions.

Kenji Nakamura: Open questions I still have:
1) In the header pill, do we show “Rolled back” forever or only for some time?
2) Do we show the “cooldown remaining” in the header?

Paula Mendes: 1) Show “Rolled back” while rollout is the active item / until rollout is closed. Once closed, in list view show a small icon + “Auto-rolled back” tag.
2) Cooldown remaining doesn’t need to be in header. In the drawer yes.

Jada Williams: Agree. Cooldown is internal policy mechanic.

Marissa Cole: Decisions:
- Verdict states: Healthy / Degraded / SLO breached / Rolling back / Rolled back / No verdict
- Replace “Primary reason” with “Triggered by” list (errors/latency/baseline)
- Details drawer includes: current value, threshold, window, min traffic, region/tier/route/model/version, links to dashboards
- Actions: Ack (only when breach/rollback), Pause (always; overflow when healthy)
- Pause requires note + duration; Ack note optional
Kenji can you update frames and tag Chloe/Jada for API field assumptions?

Kenji Nakamura: Yep, will update today and re-post.

Chloe Martin: I’ll sync with Jada on API response shape and reason_code mapping. Also will confirm wording with SRE (Degraded vs At-risk) but we’ll keep as above for now.

Hannah Rivera: Once reason strings are stable-ish, send me the label list so notifications match.

Marissa Cole: Great. Closing loop after design review.
